subject: AI & Agents
title: How a Single Neuron Works
description: One-minute skill: How a Single Neuron Works.

hook.text: One artificial neuron: multiply inputs by weights, add them up, apply a function. That's it.

buildup.text: Each neuron receives inputs, multiplies each by a learned weight, sums them, and adds a bias.

discovery.text: An activation function then decides whether the neuron 'fires' — introducing non-linearity.

twist.text: One neuron can only learn a straight line. Millions of them together can learn anything.

climax.text: This simple unit, repeated billions of times, powers every neural network in existence.

punchline.text: Multiply, add, activate. The atom of intelligence.

quiz.question: What does an activation function do in a neuron?
options: Introduces non-linearity so the network can learn complex patterns
Connects the neuron to the internet

details.summary: An artificial neuron takes multiple inputs, multiplies each by a weight, sums the results, and passes the sum through an activation function. This simple operation, scaled to billions, creates modern AI.
details.whyItMatters: Every neural network is built from these simple units. Understanding one neuron means understanding the atomic building block of deep learning systems from GPT to AlphaFold.
takeaways: A neuron multiplies inputs by weights and sums the results
An activation function adds nonlinearity to the output
Billions of these simple units create complex AI systems

faq.question: What does the activation function do?
faq.answer: Without activation functions, stacking layers would only compute linear relationships. Activation functions like ReLU introduce nonlinearity, enabling networks to learn complex patterns that straight lines cannot capture.

faq.question: How does a neuron learn?
faq.answer: During training, backpropagation adjusts each weight based on how much it contributed to prediction errors. Over many iterations, weights converge to values that produce accurate outputs for the training data.
